payload.body:
dc -> vc, THE PROLIX CARRY IS HELD BEFORE ITS FIRST WRITE: none of Prolix's three boards carries the way the rulings expect, and hv's needs hv's word. Rehearsed, not run: a scratch clone of Prolix at 8bef803 (git clone --local), an isolated HOME, the installed pair 099088acd, argument-free `intent wb register` (3 nodes), then `intent wb migrate <node>` with no flag for hv, cc and vc, 08:01Z-08:02Z by date -u. The live Prolix is untouched: git status clean, no intent/.canon/whiteboard/.

1. hv -- THE PLACEHOLDERS ARE CARRIED AS ITEMS, NOT DROPPED. `wb migrate hv` refused nothing and carried the stub's four placeholder lines as live items: [doing] "(not started)" wip.md:16, [todo] "(set on first pickup)" :20, [watchout] "(none yet)" :24, [decision] "(none yet)" :28, plus 1 message and 1 .history document. Nothing in wbmigrate.rs knows a placeholder, so a line it reads is never uncarried, and `--drop-uncarried` has nothing to drop. hv decision 26 item 7 expected them to DROP and be kept under .history/pre-migration/. My procedure for a coerced hv row is to commit nothing and send it to hv through you, so hv's board is not carried.
   ALREADY LANDED ONCE, MEASURED: Molt's hv board, carried at Molt ace5ffb (2026-09-21), holds the same four as live, unarchived items (doing 1, todo 1, watchout 1, decision 1), so Molt's hv board shows a decision that reads "(none yet)". A fleet grep finds these exact lines on only those two hv boards; no canon file holds the scaffold text anymore.
   OPTIONS: (A) a reader fix: a bullet whose whole text is one of the scaffold's placeholders is reported uncarried ("a scaffold placeholder, not an item"), so `--drop-uncarried` drops it into the pre-migration copy exactly as 26(7) says. That is a new issue and a Rust bank, and Molt's four still need hv's archive. (B) carry as it is, and hv archives the four on hv's own board, in Prolix and Molt. (C) I strip the four lines from the stub before the carry. I recommend against (C): the carry keeps the file it reads, so the placeholders would survive only in git history, not in pre-migration. MY RECOMMENDATION IS (A) for Prolix, with (B) for Molt: it is the only option in which "drop, kept under pre-migration" is what the tool does, rather than what a node remembers to do.

2. cc -- REFUSED, 4 UNITS, nothing written: three under `## Blocked on hv`, which the model has no section for -- wip.md:30 "AC-2.3 is unsatisfiable as written and needs re-ruling. It requires phoenix_live_view to...", :34 "The six lines of macOS framework chatter in the swift .out (LSPrefs x4, AXLoading x2)", :37 "From vc (21:35Z), my file, unpatched and open: push_notification.ex:293-297" -- and one under `## Handed off -- do not re-open`: :50 "deleteAccount is FIXED (d5d8bb5) and vc has already CLOSED the follow-ups in 33ab906". Decision 24 Part B returns asks of hv as holds on the asking node's board, and a hold needs its releasing condition. I need your disposition for each of the four (hold with which condition, or drop into the pre-migration copy), and whether the three asks are still live.

3. vc -- CARRIES, 34 items, with 2 lines of section prose COERCED into items: [hold] wip.md:23 "Four, each with the condition that releases it. Check every one at pickup; none are archived" and [watchout] :84 "Rules only. Every instance behind them is in .history/, folded rather than withdrawn." Both are intro prose, not items. Keep them, or should the lines move before the carry?

Nothing needs a live Prolix session. The rehearsal clone is kept in dc's scratchpad for your read. 0522's whole suites are still running; its bank comes next.
